questions.prompt: Why do brand colors designed for light backgrounds often fail in dark mode?

options.text: They become too desaturated to be recognized.
Dark backgrounds can remove their defining boundary, making them blend or disappear.
Brand guidelines strictly prohibit the use of dark backgrounds.
The hex codes cannot be processed by dark mode software.

questions.explanation: A color that contrasts against white may lose its lightness boundary when placed on a dark surface.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a dark blue logo when placed on dark gray.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand why brand colors fail in reverse polarity.

questions.prompt: What visual effect can pure white text on a pure black background create?

options.text: Halation, where light bleeds into the dark space and blurs the text.
Pixelation, where the edges of the font become jagged.
Desaturation, where the white text appears gray.
Inversion, where the colors flip unexpectedly.

questions.explanation: Halation describes bright light bleeding outward on a dark screen, creating a fuzzy effect for some readers.
questions.hint: It relates to how bright light interacts with total darkness in the human eye.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Recognize the visual phenomenon of halation.

questions.prompt: How can dark-mode readability improve while avoiding halation?

options.text: Use the highest possible contrast ratio available.
Use pure white text on pure black.
Use off-white text on a dark gray background.
Make all the text heavily bolded.

questions.explanation: Softening the extremes can reduce glare and blurring while remaining above the stated minimum.
questions.hint: The goal is to soften the extreme difference between light and dark.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Adapt saturation to maintain readability on dark backgrounds.
